When the Prophet asked who would kill Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf for harming Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad bin Maslama sought a loan, offering arms in pledge, then killed him.
Before campaigns the Prophet hid his real destination, except for Tabuk, a long march in great heat against a large enemy, when he told the Muslims so they could prepare.
The Prophet sends Ansar men against Abu Rafi; Abdullah bin Atik slips into his fort at night, kills him and, despite a sprained foot, waits to hear him mourned.
The Prophet seeks someone to kill Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf, who hurt Allah and His Apostle; allowed to say what he likes, Muhammad bin Maslama talks with Ka'b, then kills him.
Salama bin Al-Akwa cries for help, chases off Ghatafan and Fazara raiders with arrows and recovers the Prophet's she-camels; the Prophet tells him to forgive them.
After conquering a people the Prophet stayed three days in their town, and he set out for Umrah from Al-Ji'rana, where he shared out the Hunain booty.
Zaid bin Arqam says the Prophet made nineteen expeditions, seventeen of them with him, the first being al-Ashira.
The Prophet asks who will kill Ka'b bin al-Ashraf; Muhammad bin Maslama does so by a ruse; Abdullah bin Atik enters Abu Rafi's castle at night and kills him.
On the Najd expedition a bedouin draws the sleeping Prophet's sword and asks who will save him; the Prophet says 'Allah', and does not punish him.
Salama bin al-Akwa chases the Ghatafan raiders who seized the Prophet's camels at Dhi-Qarad, recovers them with his arrows, and is told by the Prophet to forgive them.
At Mu'tah, Zaid, Ja'far and Ibn Rawaha lead in turn and are martyred, Ja'far wounded only in front; the Prophet weeps, forbids the women's crying, and Khalid breaks nine swords.
Salama bin al-Akwa counts seven or nine expeditions with the Prophet, including Khaibar, al-Hudaybiya, Hunain and al-Qarad, and more under commanders such as Abu Bakr and Usama.
While besieging Ta'if the Prophet bars an effeminate man from entering upon women; when the fort holds out, his companions fight and are wounded, then gladly agree to return.
A detachment sent to Najd returns with thirteen camels each; Khalid kills and captures men of Jadhima who said 'Saba'na' instead of 'Aslamna', and the Prophet disowns what Khalid did.
Three hundred men under Abu Ubaida on the coast, reduced to a date a day and eating leaves, eat a huge fish for half a month; the Prophet eats some.
The Banu Tamim delegation asks for gifts beyond good tidings; Abu Huraira lists three qualities the Prophet ascribed to them, and Abu Bakr and Umar argue over appointing their ruler.
Abdul Qais delegates are told to believe, pray, pay Zakat, fast and give a fifth of booty, and forbidden four vessels; they delay the Prophet's two rak'at until after Asr.
Companions count the Prophet's Ghazawat: Zaid bin Arqam says nineteen, of which he joined seventeen, while al-Bara fought fifteen and Buraida sixteen with him.
Khalid killed and captured men of Bani Jadhima who could not say 'Aslamna', ordered captives killed, Ibn Umar refused, and the Prophet twice declared himself free of Khalid's deed.
